intro: A garage-punk trio from Castel Goffredo, Italy.
story: Bee Bee Sea is a garage-punk trio from Castel Goffredo, Italy, formed right out of high school. Sonic Boomerang came out in late 2017 on Dirty Water and Wild Honey, and WGBH said they play revved-up garage punk and have toured with Thee Oh Sees and Black Lips. They played Pickathon in 2018. Day Ripper followed in 2020, and in 2025 the twelve-track Stanzini Can Be Allright, an EP marking a decade together, on Wild Honey.

intro: A Toronto indie-rock collective of many hands.
story: Broken Social Scene is the Toronto collective behind You Forgot It in People, from 2002. Hug of Thunder, their fifth album and first in seven years after a hiatus declared in 2011, came out on Arts & Crafts on July 7, 2017, and NPR noted it features all 15 original members. They played Pickathon in 2018. Remember the Humans arrived in 2026 on Arts & Crafts and City Slang.

intro: Haley Fohr's four-octave voice, in experimental song.
story: Haley Fohr was born on December 16, 1988, in Lafayette, Indiana, and began Circuit des Yeux in 2007, with the debut Symphone in 2008. Reaching for Indigo, her first for Drag City, came out on October 20, 2017, co-produced with Cooper Crain, and NPR said Fohr meditates on existence with telescopic ears and eyes. She told Bandcamp Daily that Circuit des Yeux is her and she is Circuit des Yeux. She played Pickathon in 2018. The album -io followed on Matador in 2021, and Halo on the Inside in 2025.

intro: Max Clarke's Everly Brothers-minded songs from New York.
story: Max Clarke named Cut Worms after a William Blake poem, and gigged in Chicago, including in the punk band The Sueves, before basing the project in Brooklyn. The 2017 EP Alien Sunset led to Hollow Ground, his Jagjaguwar debut, produced with Jonathan Rado of Foxygen, and Bandcamp Daily said he makes 1950s doo-wop and country sounds feel radical. He played Pickathon in 2018. Nobody Lives Here Anymore followed in 2020, a self-titled album on July 21, 2023, and Transmitter, produced by Wilco's Jeff Tweedy.

intro: An Ethiopian keyboardist, back on stage after decades as a cab driver.
story: Hailu Mergia formed the Walias band in the early 1970s while working Addis Ababa's nightclubs, and moved to Washington, D.C. in the 1980s, where he drove a cab for decades. Awesome Tapes From Africa reissued his 1985 solo album Shemonmuanaye in 2013 and Tche Belew in 2014, and Lala Belu, his first studio album in 15 years, came out in 2018; Chris May of All About Jazz said it may even be better than his 1970s predecessors. He played Pickathon that summer. Yene Mircha followed in 2020.

intro: A prolific Anacortes songwriter of warm, odd indie-folk.
story: Karl Blau is a multi-instrumentalist from Anacortes, Washington, active since 1996 and part of the K Records and Knw-Yr-Own collective, now based in Philadelphia. Introducing Karl Blau, a country-covers album produced by Tucker Martine, came out on Bella Union on May 13, 2016, and NPR called it a fantastic introduction to a talented musician. XPN counted more than 40 records in about 20 years, and he has toured and recorded with Laura Veirs. He played Pickathon in 2018, after Out Her Space in 2017, and in 2026 toured the UK and the U.S. East Coast.

intro: A Tokyo psychedelic band of sitar and long jams.
story: Kikagaku Moyo began busking on the streets of Tokyo in summer 2012, and its members started the Guruguru Brain label in 2015. Masana Temples, their fourth album, came out on Guruguru Brain on October 5, 2018, recorded in Lisbon with Bruno Pernadas, and God Is in the TV called it their most focused record to date. They played Pickathon that year. Kumoyo Island followed in 2022, and the band played its last show on December 3, 2022, at Meguro Persimmon Hall in Tokyo. Go Kurosawa has since released a solo debut.

intro: A Cajun band that sets the old music to a punk pulse.
story: Brothers André and Louis Michot formed Lost Bayou Ramblers in 1999 in Pilette, Louisiana, and their 2001 debut was Pilette Breakdown. Kalenda came out on Rice Pump on September 26, 2017, and won the Grammy for Best Regional Roots Music Album at the January 2018 ceremony, seven months before they played Pickathon. Live: Orpheum Theater NOLA, with the Louisiana Philharmonic Orchestra, was nominated in 2024.
artist_reel_line: Live: Orpheum Theater NOLA was a 2024 Grammy nominee.

story: Low Cut Connie is the Philadelphia band built around the pianist Adam Weiner. Barack Obama put "Boozophilia" on his 2015 summer Spotify playlist, and Elton John interviewed Weiner on his radio show in 2017. Dirty Pictures (Part 1) came out in May 2017 and Part 2 on May 18, 2018, both on Contender Records, the year they played Pickathon. The double album Private Lives followed in 2020, Art Dealers in 2023, and Livin In The USA, their eighth studio album, in 2026.

intro: A Portland guitarist of deep solo fingerpicking.
story: Marisa Anderson is a Portland guitarist whose Cloud Corner, her first for Thrill Jockey and sixth solo album, was recorded at home in January 2017 and came out on June 15, 2018; NPR's First Listen called her one of the era's most powerful players. She played Pickathon that summer. The Quickening, with Jim White, followed in 2020, Lost Futures, with William Tyler, in 2021, Still, Here in 2022, and The Anthology of UnAmerican Folk Music in 2026.

intro: A songwriter who rebuilds old ballads.
story: Sam Amidon was born on June 3, 1981, in Brattleboro, Vermont, to the folk-singing parents Peter and Mary Alice Amidon, who had performed with Bread and Puppet Theater. His Nonesuch run began with Bright Sunny South in 2013, then Lily-O in 2014, which The Independent gave four stars, and The Following Mountain in 2017, his first with all original songs. He played Pickathon in 2015 and 2018. A self-titled album of nine traditional-song takes came out on October 23, 2020, Salt River in 2025 and Willows in 2026.
artist_reel_line: Willing Brother Knowing, due in February 2027, is produced by James Krivchenia.

intro: A Philadelphia band of punchy, political punk-pop.
story: Sheer Mag formed in Philadelphia in 2014 and built a following on 7-inch EPs, avoiding press until their debut album. Need to Feel Your Love came out on Wilsuns Recording Company on July 14, 2017, produced by Hart Seely, and The Guardian, NME and DIY each gave it five stars; its title track became Bernie Sanders's walkout song at a rally. They played Pickathon in 2018. A Distant Call followed in 2019, and Playing Favorites on Third Man in 2024.

intro: A New York trio in the first flush of their name.
story: Sunflower Bean is the Brooklyn trio of Julia Cumming, Nick Kivlen and Jacob Faber, formed in 2014, first on Fat Possum before Mom + Pop. Twentytwo in Blue came out on March 23, 2018, when all three members were 22, and The Line of Best Fit made it Album of the Week. They played Pickathon in 2017 and again in 2018. Headful of Sugar followed in 2022 and Mortal Primetime, self-produced, in 2025.
